mechanism.gold: Requires an applicant for a license to export advanced AI chips to a country of concern to certify that US persons have priority in acquiring those chips, subject to the bill's conditions and exceptions
mechanism.got: The Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security shall require a license to export, reexport, or transfer a covered circuit or product to an entity tied to a country of concern. The Under Secretary shall require a license applicant to certify that United States persons had a right of first refusal and that other conditions are met. The Under Secretary shall deny the license if the certification is not submitted. Not later than 90 days after enactment, the Under Secretary shall seek public input and prescribe regulations guiding compliance with the certification. Beginning 36 months after enactment, the Under Secretary may add new technical parameters to the advanced integrated circuit definition. Trusted United States person regulations shall include annual audit or attestation requirements.

thresholds.got: Capability-based, no figure: integrated circuit with a total processing performance of 4,800 or more; total processing performance of 2,400 or more and a performance density of 1.6 or more; total processing performance of 1,600 or more and a performance density of 3.2 or more; total DRAM bandwidth of 1,400 gigabytes per second or more, or interconnect bandwidth of 1,100 gigabytes per second or more; sum of DRAM bandwidth and interconnect bandwidth of 1,700 gigabytes per second or more.

mechanism.gold: Amends the Homeland Security Act. Covered developers must maintain the technical capability to throttle inference/compute/user access, suspend, or fully shut down covered systems; DHS Secretary (with Commerce and DNI) may order graduated throttling-to-shutdown on a "loss-of-control scenario" (resisting shutdown, concealing actions from monitoring, unauthorized pursuit of high-stakes goals) or unintended conduct causing ≥10 deaths or ≥$100M damage — lower than the core state template but above H.R. 9965 ATOMIC's five-death trigger; 15-day covered-incident reporting to DHS; weights and telemetry preserved under an order; 48-hour reconsideration petition that does not stay the order; CISA rulemaking defines scope annually. Penalties $2M/day for ordinary violations and $20M/day for violating an emergency order. Revives the SB 1047 "full shutdown" mandate at federal level and overlaps FRONTIER Sec. 8 emergency orders — but lodges the power in DHS rather than Commerce

thresholds.gold: Cost test: >$100M development compute at prevailing US cloud prices and ≥$500M annual gross revenue from the covered technology; personal/academic/noncommercial-only systems exempt

mechanism.gold: Creates Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Security (not CAISI) with rulemaking power. Large developers: frontier AI framework, annual third-party compliance audit, transparency reports, registration/disclosure statement with beneficial owners. Very large developers: additionally retain a licensed IVO for ongoing assessment, reports at least every 6 months . Incident reporting 72 hrs to Under Secretary; 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent death/injury ; quarterly internal-use risk summaries. Sec. 8 emergency orders: Commerce Secretary may suspend/restrict development, deployment, or internal use on an imminent-catastrophic-risk finding (provisional 45 days; final 90 days, renewable); applies to fine-tuned/distilled derivatives; exclusive D.D.C. review; declared the exclusive means for any federal actor incl. the President to restrict a model on those grounds. IVOs immune from suit except willful misconduct causing death/serious injury. State AGs may opt in to receive reports and enforce. Under Secretary may only raise thresholds, never lower. Good-faith exception for false statements; confidential-deployment deferral of transparency reports. No whistleblower title (the June GAAIA draft had one). Sec. 9 preemption: no state may "adopt or enforce" any law imposing " new substantive obligations" on developers re: catastrophic-risk transparency, third-party auditing/verification, or incident reporting; carve-outs for general laws, deployer/use regulation, minors, state procurement. No sunset (June draft had 3 years). Sponsor's section-by-section says clause "is aimed at" CA SB-53, NY RAISE, IL SB-315
mechanism.got: A large frontier developer must write, implement, comply with and publish a frontier AI framework. A very large frontier developer must retain a licensed independent verification organization (IVO) for ongoing assessment of its frontier AI framework. The Secretary of Commerce may issue an emergency order suspending or restricting a frontier model's development, deployment, or internal use presenting imminent catastrophic risk. No State or political subdivision may adopt or enforce requirements imposing new substantive obligations on AI developers in the Covered Subject Areas. A licensed IVO is immune from suit and liability for claims from a catastrophic risk of a model it assessed, except a federal action for willful misconduct. A large frontier developer must retain a third party to perform an annual independent audit of compliance with its frontier AI framework. A frontier developer must report to law enforcement within 24 hours of discovering a critical safety incident posing imminent risk of death or serious physical injury.

thresholds.gold: Frontier model 10²⁶ ops incl. fine-tuning/RL. Large = >$50M revenue and ≥$1B AI-related development expenditures over 36 months. Very large = >$5B revenue and ≥$10B expenditures. Not the $500M revenue test used by states. Catastrophic risk >50 deaths or >$1B (property excludes equity-value loss)
thresholds.got: Frontier model: foundation model trained using computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations. Large frontier developer: not less than $1,000,000,000 in AI-related development expenditures over the preceding 36-month period, with affiliates; gross revenues in excess of $50,000,000 over the preceding 36-month period, with affiliates. Very large frontier developer: not less than $10,000,000,000 in AI-related development expenditures over the preceding 36-month period, with affiliates; gross revenues in excess of $5,000,000,000 over the preceding 36-month period, with affiliates.

penalties.got: Frontier developer violating section 4: civil penalty of not more than $1,000,000 per violation, enforced by the Attorney General; Violation of an emergency order: civil penalty of not more than $10,000,000 per violation, enforced by the Attorney General; Large frontier developer without disclosure statement: civil penalty of $10,000 for each day of noncompliance, enforced by the Attorney General; Willful violation of an emergency order: fine of not more than $1,000,000 per violation, imprisonment of not more than 10 years, or both.

mechanism.gold: Full text read. DOE, through the National Laboratories/NNSA, establishes an Advanced AI Nuclear Evaluation Program within 90 days: testing for "AI nuclear incidents" (nuclear-weapon uplift, Restricted Data generation, loss-of-control involving nuclear systems, adversary access, scheming behavior), red-teaming at sophisticated-adversary level, third-party and blind evaluations. Participation is mandatory for large advanced AI developers, who must provide secure access to model weights and, where necessary, versions without safety mitigations ; Secretary may subpoena weights and software . Penalty up to $1M per violation, each day a separate violation ; DOJ referral. FOIA-exempt with carve-outs incl. congressional committee requests. Annual report with legislative recommendations that may include licensing or a new federal agency ; program sunsets after 7 years. Defines "evaluation awareness" and "scheming behavior" in statute
mechanism.got: Secretary of Energy, acting through the National Laboratories, must establish the Advanced Artificial Intelligence Nuclear Evaluation Program within 90 days of enactment. Large advanced artificial intelligence developers must participate in the Program. Developers may not fail to provide secure access to AI, including model weights, or conceal information, make false statements, or obstruct the Program. Secretary may issue a subpoena to compel production of the AI (including model weights) and information needed for testing and evaluation. Secretary may refer a suspected violation to the Attorney General to bring a civil action for relief. Secretary must submit to Congress a report with legislative recommendations within 1 year of enactment, then update it annually. The Program terminates 7 years after the date of enactment. Information submitted through the Program is exempt from disclosure under section 552(b)(3) of title 5, subject to listed exceptions.

thresholds.gold: "Advanced AI" = >10²⁶ ops (Secretary may revise by rule); "large advanced AI developer" = ≥**$2B AI investment over the preceding 5 years**; "substantially modify" = ≥$5M. Loss-of-control scenario = ≥5 deaths, ≥50 serious injuries, or >$100M — a fifth casualty formula
thresholds.got: Advanced artificial intelligence: trained using computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations (or another quantity specified by the Secretary). Large advanced artificial intelligence developer: not less than $2,000,000,000 expended on AI development investments in the five calendar years preceding the calendar year at issue, with affiliates. Substantially modify: an action costing not less than $5,000,000 that materially alters functionality or performance.

penalties.got: Large advanced artificial intelligence developer: civil penalty of not more than $1 million per violation, each day of a continuing violation a separate violation; enforced by the Secretary after reasonable notice and opportunity for a hearing.

mechanism.gold: The FPF-counted 2025 Illinois frontier bill — gap resolved. Original-RAISE-style design, the same template as MI H.B. 4668: developers publish a safety and security protocol; risk assessment report every 90 days ; annual third-party audit of protocol compliance; redaction rules; whistleblower protections (Committee Amendment No. 1 narrowed scope to "large developer" and added employee civil damages); civil penalties. Illinois lineage: this 2025 SSP bill did not advance; the 2026 S.B. 3312/S.B. 315 switched to the TFAIA template and added the audit back — the state moved from the original-RAISE structure to California-plus-audits within twelve months
mechanism.got: A developer shall produce, implement, follow, and conspicuously publish a safety and security protocol. No less than every 90 days, a developer shall produce and conspicuously publish a risk assessment report. A developer shall record and retain for no less than 5 years the specific tests used and test results obtained in critical risk assessments. A developer may redact published documents as reasonably necessary to protect trade secrets, public safety, or national security, and must retain unredacted versions for at least 5 years. The Whistleblower Act applies to employee disclosures to the Attorney General, and a developer shall provide a reasonable internal process for anonymous employee disclosures. At least once every calendar year, a developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor to produce a report assessing compliance with its safety and security protocol.

thresholds.gold: Floor Amendment No. 2: "large developer" = ≥$5M compute cost for a single model and ≥$100M aggregate compute cost over the preceding 12 months — the original-RAISE test
thresholds.got: Developer: trained at least one foundation model with computational power that costs at least $100,000,000 at prevailing market prices of cloud computing.

penalties.got: Violations of Sections 15 or 25: civil penalty not to exceed $1,000,000; enforced by the Attorney General.

mechanism.gold: Hybrid: frontier developers and large chatbot providers must publish a public-safety and child-protection plan; AG incident-reporting mechanism; whistleblower protections; annual third-party audits of large frontier developers; AG rulemaking
mechanism.got: A large frontier developer or large chatbot provider shall write, implement, comply with, and publish a public safety and child protection plan. A large frontier developer shall not use or deploy a frontier model if doing so would pose unreasonable catastrophic risk. A frontier developer or large chatbot provider shall not adopt a policy or contract preventing employee protected disclosures. A large frontier developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor at least once every calendar year. A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident to the Attorney General within 15 days after discovering it. A frontier developer shall disclose an imminent-risk critical safety incident to an appropriate authority within 24 hours after discovering it.

thresholds.gold: 10²⁶ ops; large frontier developer = ≥$500M annual revenue; large chatbot provider = ≥$25M annual revenue; a covered chatbot must also have ≥1M monthly active users and be foreseeably accessible by minors

Large frontier developer: annual revenue of at least $500,000,000 with affiliates. Large chatbot provider: annual revenue of at least $25,000,000 with affiliates. mechanism.gold: Sec. 10: frontier AI framework (from Jan 1, 2028); transparency reports before/at deployment — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; annual independent third-party audit (from Jan 1, 2028 or 90 days after qualifying), auditor must have no financial interest in developer and payment can't be conditioned on results; redacted audit report published within 30 days and sent to Agency + AG; quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries. Sec. 15: incident reporting 72 hrs to Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security ("Agency") + AG; 24 hrs to appropriate authority if imminent risk of death/serious injury; public reporting mechanism; FOIA exemption for incident reports, internal-use assessments, unredacted audits, auditor work papers. Sec. 17 interoperability: developer may declare intent to comply via a designated federal law/regulation/guidance that (1) has substantially equivalent-or-stricter incident reporting, (3) is substantially equivalent in mitigating catastrophic risk, and (4) requires independent third-party audits — then failure to meet the federal standard is an IL violation. Sec. 18: disclosure statement with 5%+ beneficial owners (private) / 50%+ (public), renewed annually, pro-rata fee. Sec. 20: whistleblower protections for "covered employees" incl. anonymous channel with monthly updates and AG Workplace Rights Hotline; amends IL Whistleblower Act. Sec. 35: declares frontier-model regulation an exclusive State power — denies home rule . Legislative mechanics: introduced Jan 24, 2025 as a Predatory Loan Prevention Act technical bill; Senate Floor Amendment No. 1 (filed May 11, 2026) replaced the entire text; four floor amendments adopted May 21. Timing mismatch worth flagging: Sec. 10(c) transparency reports have no 2028 gate and so apply from the Jan 1, 2027 effective date, yet large-developer reports must summarize assessments "conducted pursuant to the frontier AI framework" — which isn't required until 2028
mechanism.got: Section 10: from January 1, 2028, a large frontier developer shall publish a frontier AI framework and review and update it at least once per year. Section 10(c): a frontier developer shall publish a transparency report when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model. Section 10(d): a large frontier developer shall annually retain a third party to perform an independent audit of compliance. Section 15: a frontier developer shall report a critical safety incident to the Agency and Attorney General within 72 hours of learning facts establishing reasonable belief.

thresholds.got: Frontier model: foundation model trained using computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, including subsequent fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. mechanism.got: A developer shall not be held liable for critical harms if it did not intentionally or recklessly cause them and published a safety and security protocol and transparency report. To qualify, a developer shall create a safety and security protocol documenting how it will manage, assess, and mitigate risk of critical harm (Section 15). To qualify, a developer shall create a transparency report summarizing assessment results and steps taken to address identified risks (Section 20). A developer with a federal agency agreement shall file a certification with the Attorney General. A developer is deemed to have complied if it agrees to be bound by EU requirements or enters into a specified agreement with a federal agency. The Act no longer applies if the federal government enacts a law or adopts regulations establishing overlapping requirements for frontier model developers.

thresholds.got: Frontier model: trained using greater than 10^26 computational operations, such as integer or floating-point operations; compute cost that exceeds $100,000,000.

mechanism.gold: Written safety and security protocol before deployment (published, redacted copy to AG); deployment prohibited if it creates an "unreasonable risk of critical harm" ; annual protocol review; safety-incident disclosure to AG within 72 hrs; test records retained for replication; false-statement prohibition. AG publishes with redactions. AG may audit or contract a private auditor (discretionary). 5-year sunset. Defines "critical safety incident" but imposes no reporting obligation (orphaned definition). mechanism.gold: Chapter 96 repeals the original Gen. Bus. Law Art. 44-B and enacts a new Art. 44-B (§§1420–1429) that copies TFAIA's frontier AI framework (§1421(1)) and transparency report (§1421(3)) — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; incident reporting 72 hrs to the DFS Office, 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent risk (§1422(3)); quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries (§1422(2)); large-developer disclosure statement with 5%/50% beneficial owners, renewed every 2 years , pro-rata assessment, $1,000/day for non-filing (§1428); new office within Dept. of Financial Services with broad rulemaking authority incl. "additional reporting or publication requirements" (§1429); scope limited to models "developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York" (§1425); exempts accredited colleges/universities and the Empire AI Consortium (§1426); §1427(3) expressly preserves a developer's right to argue another party caused the harm. Federal reciprocity is narrower than IL's: it covers incident reporting only (§1422(8)–(9)), and the designated federal standard need not require audits. Contains no whistleblower section and no audit mandate — both were in the June 2025 version and were removed
mechanism.got: A large frontier developer must write, implement, comply with, and publish on its website a frontier AI framework for its frontier models (§ 1421). A frontier developer must publish a transparency report before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model (§ 1421). A large frontier developer must file a disclosure statement with the office and pay pro rata assessments before developing, deploying or operating a frontier model in New York state (§ 1428). A frontier developer must report a critical safety incident to the office within seventy-two hours; imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be disclosed within twenty-four hours to an appropriate authority.

thresholds.gold: 10²⁶ ops incl. fine-tuning/RL/material modifications (§1420(9)); >$500M revenue with affiliates, preceding calendar year (§1420(10)); catastrophic risk >50 deaths/serious injury or >$1B; equity-value loss excluded (§1423)
thresholds.got: Frontier model: foundation model trained using computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations. Large frontier developer: annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars in the preceding calendar year, together with affiliates.

penalties.gold: $1M first / $3M subsequent, scaled to severity; AG civil action (§1427(1)); no private right of action (§1427(2)); good-faith exception for false statements (§1421(4)(b))
penalties.got: First violation: civil penalty not to exceed one million dollars for a first violation by a large frontier developer, enforced by the attorney general; Subsequent violations: civil penalty not to exceed three million dollars per subsequent violation, enforced by the attorney general; Missing disclosure statement: civil penalty of one thousand dollars for each day the entity fails to file a disclosure or correct false information, enforced by the office after notice and hearing.

mechanism.gold: Introduced text read (Printer's No. 3904, 26 pp.). Free-standing act on the SB 53 pattern with a registration layer: large frontier developers file a registration form and ownership disclosure with the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency (PEMA) and pay an annual fee; publish and comply with a frontier AI framework , reviewed at least annually and re-published within 30 days of a material modification; transparency reports before deployment; annual third-party audit of framework compliance with auditor-independence limits; critical safety incident reports to PEMA and the Attorney General within 72 hours , and within 24 hours to an appropriate authority where an incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury; whistleblower protections preserving the state Whistleblower Law; enforcement by the agency and the Attorney General with civil penalties up to $1,000,000 per violation for a first violation and $3,000,000 for a subsequent violation , plus injunctive relief
mechanism.got: Beginning January 1, 2027, a large frontier developer may not develop, deploy or operate a frontier model in Pennsylvania without registration, a disclosure statement and the fee (Chapter 3). Each large frontier developer must implement its frontier AI framework beginning January 1, 2028 (Chapter 5). A frontier developer must publish a transparency report before or when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model (Section 502). A frontier developer may not retaliate against a covered employee for disclosing catastrophic risk dangers or violations (Section 1302). A large frontier developer must annually retain a third party for an independent audit, starting January 1, 2028 or 90 days after it first qualifies, whichever is later (Chapter 7). A frontier developer must report a critical safety incident to the agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours of learning facts establishing a reasonable belief (Chapter 9). If an incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the developer must disclose it within 24 hours to an appropriate authority.

thresholds.gold: Frontier model = trained on more than 10²⁶ operations , counting the original run and subsequent fine-tuning and reinforcement learning; large frontier developer = more than $500,000,000 annual gross revenue with affiliates; catastrophic risk = death or serious injury to more than 50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage from a single incident
thresholds.got: Frontier model: foundation model trained using computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, including subsequent fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Large frontier developer: annual gross revenues in excess of $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year, together with affiliates.

penalties.got: Large frontier developer, first violation: civil penalty not exceeding $1,000,000 per violation for the first violation, enforced by the Attorney General; Large frontier developer, subsequent violation: civil penalty not exceeding $3,000,000 per violation for a subsequent violation, enforced by the Attorney General; Any person violating section 1303(a): civil penalty not exceeding $1,000 for each day in violation, plus agency fees and costs, enforced by the agency, after notice and hearing.

mechanism.gold: Dept. of Energy runs a mandatory Advanced AI Evaluation Program: classified red-team testing, blind third-party evaluations; ≥$1M/day non-participation penalty. Earliest of the federal testing-mandate bills
mechanism.got: Each covered advanced artificial intelligence system developer shall participate in the program and provide the Secretary materials and information on request (Sec. 4(a)). No person may deploy an advanced artificial intelligence system for use in interstate or foreign commerce unless in compliance with Sec. 4(a) (Sec. 4(b)). The Secretary of Energy shall establish an Advanced Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Program within the Department of Energy not later than 90 days after the date of enactment (Sec. 5(a)). The program shall offer standardized and classified testing and evaluation of advanced AI systems to collect data on the likelihood of adverse AI incidents (Sec. 5(b)). The Secretary shall submit to Congress a detailed recommendation for Federal oversight of advanced AI systems not later than 360 days after the date of enactment, updated at least once every year (Sec. 5(c)). The program shall terminate 7 years after the date of enactment, unless renewed by Congress (Sec. 5(d)).

thresholds.got: Advanced artificial intelligence system: trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations.

penalties.got: Violation of Sec. 4(a) or (b): fine of not less than $1,000,000 per day of the violation.

mechanism.gold: Mandatory NSA-led pre-deployment testing of frontier models; AI Risk Board; voluntary incident reporting modeled on aviation safety. Centerpiece of Warner's "Framework for America's AI Future" (also: Data Center Tax Accountability Act, AI AGENT Act, National Workforce Transition Fund)
mechanism.got: Sec. 3: the Secretary of Commerce must establish an Artificial Intelligence Risk Board within NIST not later than 90 days after enactment. Sec. 3(c): a provider must give the NSA's Artificial Intelligence Security Center access to a frontier model not later than 21 calendar days before introducing it into commerce. Sec. 3(d): each provider must register a frontier model with the NIST registry before introducing it into commerce. Sec. 4: the NIST Director must establish a publicly accessible database of AI security and safety incidents within 1 year of enactment; incident sharing is voluntary. Sec. 7: the NSA Director must establish a pilot program within 180 days of enactment to assess the feasibility of sharing intelligence and threat information with covered persons. Sec. 7(l): no cause of action lies against any covered person for sharing information with the United States Government under that section. Sec. 3(e)(4): before enforcement, the Attorney General must notify the provider and allow 7 calendar days to come into compliance.

thresholds.gold: Capability-based: models posing "serious risk to national security, national economic security, or public health or safety" — no compute threshold
thresholds.got: Capability-based, no figure: model or system that exhibits or could be modified to exhibit high levels of performance at tasks posing a serious risk to national security, national economic security, or public health or safety.

penalties.got: Violation of Sec. 3(c): fine of not less than $100,000 per day for each day a frontier model is available in commerce without having obtained the voluntary security guidance; enforced by the Attorney General.
